HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIKAS MAHAJAN  ORDER % 16.10.2023 CRL.M.A. 27740/2023 (exemption)
1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The present petition has been filed under Section 482 CrPC seeking quashing of FIR No.
222/2020 under Section 324 IPC registered at Police Station Mansarovar Park, on the ground that the parties have arrived at a settlement.

Subsequently, charge was framed under Sections 324/354 IPC by the learned Trial Court vide order dated 11.04.2022.
4.
Issue notice.
The learned APP for the State accepts notice.
He submits that since the FIR is an outcome of a matrimonial dispute and the parties have arrived at a settlement, the State has no objection in case the FIR in question is quashed.
5. The petitioner (former husband), as well as, respondent no. 2 (former This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 18/10/2023 at 22:27:23 wife) are present in Court and they have been identified by their counsel and by ASI Kadeer Ahmad,
PS. M.S. Park.
6. The brief facts of the case are that the marriage between the petitioner and respondent no. 2 was solemnized on 21.02.2017 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies.
No child was born out of the said wedlock.

sentences.text: On account of temperamental issues, certain disputes arose between the parties and they started living separately w.e.f. 20.09.2020.
The dispute between the parties also led to the registration of present FIR.
8. Apart from the aforesaid FIR, another FIR was also registered at the instance of respondent no.2 being FIR No. 1181/2021 under Sections 498A/406/377/34 IPC.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that another petition seeking quashing of this FIR is also listed today before a Coordinate Bench of this Court.

9. During the pendency of the proceedings the parties arrived at a settlement, terms whereof were reduced in writing in the form of Memorandum of Understanding dated 01.06.2022, copy of which is annexed as Annexure P-3 to the present petition.
10. In terms of the said settlement, the petitioner and the respondent no. 2 decided to dissolve their marriage by filing a petition for divorce by way of mutual consent.
Accordingly, they have obtained a decree of divorce dated 03.02.2023, which is annexed as Annexure P-5 to the present petition.

11. It is also a term of the settlement between the parties that the petitioner will pay a total sum of Rs.8 lacs to the respondent no.2 as full and final settlement towards all her claims on account of streedhan, permanent alimony, dowry articles and maintenance (past, present and future) etc.
12.
Out of the said amount, a sum of Rs.5 lacs has already been paid by
This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 18/10/2023 at 22:27:23 the petitioner to the respondent no.2 in the manner as mentioned in the settlement.

Further, an amount of Rs.2.5 lacs is to be paid at the time of quashing of aforesaid FIR No. 1181/2021 and the remaining amount of Rs. 50,000/- has been paid to the respondent no.2 today in court by the petitioner by way of Demand Draft bearing No.172600 dated 04.10.2023 issued by Bank of Baroda,
Mandoli, New Delhi, in favour of Archana.

13. The receipt of part settlement amount of Rs.5.5 lacs is acknowledged by the respondent no.2,
who is present in Court.
14. The respondent no.2, on a query put by the Court, states that she has no objection in case the FIR is quashed.
15. In view of the fact that the parties have arrived at a settlement, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
16. It is, thus, in the interest of justice that the present FIR and all the other proceedings emanating therefrom be quashed.
